video.title: "find your passion" is bad advice. the science behind why & what to do instead

protocol.status: v2 labeler B (rubric v2), independent of A
protocol.note: Drafted from the transcript alone, without seeing any jevcut output or other labels.
protocol.times_from: Lemonfox transcript; seconds in the source, so labels survive re-transcription

clips.why: Hook: in 2018 three Stanford researchers (Dweck, Walton, O'Keefe) studied why people looking for their passion never find one: not a discovery problem, a mindset problem - passions are 'found' vs 'built', fixed vs growth theory of interest. Payoff: what you believe about passion predicts whether you find one (135.0). 111.3 (found vs built) is the shortest acceptable end. Skip the leading 'So,'.

People who think passions are found expect 'boundless motivation'; when it gets dull their brain runs 'if this were really my passion it wouldn't be so difficult' and they abandon it (167.8). Running on through the built-mindset contrast to 187.1 also works.

Mistake: saying 'I want to become a YouTuber / writer' - identity statements feel high stakes and your brain freezes. Instead Anne-Laure Le Cunff's 'pact': a specific action for a specific duration, 'I will write a thousand words every weekend for four weeks' (398.2-400.0). The YouTube pact example to 'That is a pact' (411.5) is the latest acceptable end. Opens on 'Step number two: run a tiny experiment' for context; 356.6 ('this is where most people make a mistake') also works.

Hot take: we hear stories of people obsessed with one instrument or sport, but that's rare; most of us have multiple passions over a life, so the pressure to find the one thing is 'mostly fiction' (512.4). Ends before the subscribe ask.

also_ok.why: Her story of never knowing her passion, being jealous of a friend's certainty, taking personality tests - until Stanford research showed it's a mindset problem, not a discovery problem. Story-shaped, a bit long.
'What am I envious of?' Envy is a signal of genuine desires (friend who became a full-time writer). Short and list-framed ('Number two'), near the bottom of the band.

negatives.why: Cold-open hook ('passions are not found; they're built') into the channel intro.
Write 20 interests; 'here's how my own list looks' reads the screen.
AdSense won't monetize her channel - tangent and a comment ask.
Rules of a good pact: needs the pact defined before.
Step three, read the data at the end of 'your pact' - depends on earlier steps; the '4 weeks vs 4 years' line alone is too short.
